strengths: Clear identification and visualization of two key problems affecting TTFS networks (signal diminishing and imbalanced membrane potential distribution) with empirical evidence
Theoretically grounded initialization method derived from first principles, showing why Kaiming initialization fails (D(X^l) ∝ 1/T) and providing principled solution (σ²_W = T/n)
Comprehensive gradient analysis (Figure 5) demonstrating dramatic improvement in gradient magnitude (1e-6 to 1e-2) with proposed initialization
Well-structured ablation study (Table III) clearly showing cumulative contributions of initialization and pooling components
Clear presentation with effective visualizations of the core problems and solutions
weaknesses: Evaluation severely limited to only MNIST and Fashion-MNIST (toy datasets by 2026 standards); no results on CIFAR-10, ImageNet, or neuromorphic benchmarks; insufficient for ICML standards

Improvements are marginal and lack statistical validation: MNIST +0.6% over TQTTFS (98.6%→99.2%), Fashion-MNIST improvements unclear due to different architectures; no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests across any result

Core theoretical assumption (exactly one spike per neuron in Eq. 20) is strong and unjustified; paper acknowledges the assumption but provides only hand-wavy justification that 'ignoring the last firing does not impact performance' without empirical validation

Temporal weighting method lacks rigor: missing Section IV-C referenced for γ ablation study, no isolated ablation of temporal weighting component, mechanism for improving BPTT gradient flow unclear, terminology issue ('logspace decay' typically means log-spacing but γ^-t is exponential decay)

No measurements of actual efficiency despite title claiming 'Efficient Training Framework': missing energy consumption analysis, latency measurements, spike count comparisons, and training time comparisons
Pooling argument (Section III-E) is superficial: notation confusing, assumptions about neuron distribution not validated, no baseline with max-pooling + new initialization for fair comparison
Missing critical ablations: no separate temporal weighting ablation, no analysis of γ hyperparameter values, incomplete evaluation of pooling alone
Network depth not evaluated: Figure 4 shows only 5-layer network; scalability to modern deep architectures (ResNet-depth) unexplored, questioning practical applicability
Reproducibility concerns: minimal hyperparameter details, no random seed handling specification, no code availability mentioned, no statement of number of experimental runs

strengths: Clear identification of two concrete training issues (signal diminishing and imbalanced membrane potential) with effective visualizations and empirical evidence
Sound variance-based mathematical derivation of the initialization scheme (σ²_W = T/n) that adapts principles to TTFS-specific constraints
Demonstrated empirical improvements in convergence speed, training stability, and accuracy on tested datasets (Figs. 4, 8-9)
Systematic analysis with good visualizations comparing Kaiming vs. proposed initialization across network depth
weaknesses: Critical theoretical gap: The initialization derivation assumes exactly one spike per neuron during training, but this inference-time property is not guaranteed during training. The dismissal of this issue is insufficient and undermines the theoretical foundation

Severely limited experimental scope: Only MNIST and Fashion-MNIST are tested. For a top-tier venue, evaluation on CIFAR-10, ImageNet, and neuromorphic datasets (DVS) is essential. Claims of 'state-of-the-art' are meaningful only for toy datasets

Limited novelty: Weight initialization for SNNs already exists (Rossbroich et al. [55]); temporal weighting w[t]=γ^(-t) is standard exponential decay; average vs. max pooling is straightforward engineering. This reads as an engineering contribution rather than research advance

Temporal weighting method lacks principled justification: The claim that initial spikes carry most information is asserted without proof. The mentioned ablation study comparing linear vs. exponential decay (Section IV-C) is referenced but not shown. Choice of γ=2 is unjustified

Critical missing validation of efficiency claims: Despite TTFS motivation (reduced spikes, energy, latency), the paper provides no spike count measurements, actual latency on hardware, or energy consumption comparisons. Only mentions '8 time steps' without baseline comparison

Pooling analysis is oversimplified: Max-pooling operates on spatial dimensions while single-spike constraint applies temporally. Equations 24-25 conflate these dimensions. Ablation shows only 1.1% improvement (89.3% to 90.35%), which is marginal

Marginal improvements over strong baselines: MNIST shows 98.6% (TQTTFS) to 99.2% improvement with unexplained asterisk. Fashion-MNIST shows only 1.2% improvement over TQTTFS. These are within noise for small datasets

Incomplete ablation studies: Only ablates two components on Fashion-MNIST. Missing: γ parameter ablation, linear vs. exponential decay comparison (mentioned but not shown), depth-dependent analysis, MNIST ablation
Insufficient comparison with related work: No direct experimental comparison with Rossbroich et al. [55] on SNN initialization. Limited discussion of specific improvements over recent TTFS methods

Gradient analysis is incomplete: Figure 5 shows larger gradients with proposed initialization, but absolute magnitudes remain very small (~1e-2). No analysis of temporal gradient flow or vanishing gradient behavior across time
Missing implementation details: No code availability mentioned; hyperparameter selection process not described; sparse reproducibility information despite using SpikingJelly
Presentation issues: Typos ('phenonmenon' p.1, 'seem' vs 'see'), unexplained asterisk in results table, claims of 'accelerating training' based only on convergence curves not wall-clock time

strengths: Clear identification and visualization of two fundamental problems (signal diminishing and imbalanced membrane potential distribution) with compelling evidence in Figures 1-2
Theoretically motivated initialization derivation (Equations 14-21) that correctly addresses TTFS-specific dynamics, yielding σ²_W = T/n
Strong experimental evidence of improvements: gradients ~10^4x larger with proposed initialization (Figure 5), faster convergence (Figure 4), demonstrated across multiple layers
Comprehensive framework addressing multiple aspects (initialization, temporal weighting, pooling) rather than a narrow fix
Achieves competitive or state-of-the-art results on tested benchmarks (99.2% on MNIST, 91.61% on Fashion-MNIST SCNN)
weaknesses: Evaluation severely limited to only MNIST and Fashion-MNIST—nearly saturated benchmarks inadequate for ICML. Modern neuromorphic (DVS-CIFAR, DVS128) and image (CIFAR-10/100) datasets required
Critical missing evaluation: no spike counts, latency, or actual energy consumption metrics despite energy efficiency being the core motivation for TTFS
Marginal improvements over SOTA (0.6% on MNIST, 1.2% on Fashion-MNIST SMLP) with no statistical significance testing, confidence intervals, or multiple runs
Limited architectural scope: only shallow networks tested (2-3 layers) despite initialization motivated by depth issues; no evaluation on genuinely deep SNNs (5+ layers)

Questionable theoretical assumption: Equation 20 assumes exactly one spike per neuron per timestep, enforced artificially by setting final threshold to -∞; claim that 'ignoring last spike does not impact performance' lacks rigorous justification

Incomplete ablation study: only on Fashion-MNIST (not MNIST), doesn't isolate temporal weighting contribution, missing sensitivity analysis for γ parameter, claimed ablation in Section IV-C comparing decay functions not shown
Arbitrary hyperparameter choice: γ=2 in weighting function presented without justification or sensitivity analysis
Pooling strategy analysis superficial: Section III-E brief, mathematical arguments incomplete, missing empirical comparison on same networks
Reproducibility concerns: code availability not mentioned, limited experimental details, single runs without error bars or multiple seeds
Generalization uncertain: only LIF neurons tested; applicability to other neuron models (IF, PLIF) unclear

strengths: Sound mathematical analysis of signal diminishing in TTFS SNNs, with rigorous variance analysis justifying ETTFS-init (Eqs. 9-15 correctly identify D(X^l) ∝ 1/T problem)

Strong experimental results with substantial improvements over prior direct-training methods (10.56% on CIFAR10, 6.94% on DVS Gesture) and comprehensive ablation studies demonstrating component effectiveness
Excellent reproducibility: detailed experimental settings (Table 6), network architectures (Table 7), and supplementary code/weights provided for full reproduction
Significant latency reductions demonstrated across datasets (Table 2, with inference time-steps reduced from 2.93 to 1.01 on MNIST)
Mathematically sound pooling analysis correctly showing max-pooling violates one-spike constraint while average-pooling preserves it
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (Figures 1-3) and comprehensive supplementary derivations
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: ETTFS-init is straightforward variance scaling (σ²_W = T/N_l); weight normalization applies existing techniques [76-78] without innovation; temporal weighting is simple exponential/linear decay; pooling analysis is observational rather than methodologically novel
Fragmented contribution structure: four somewhat independent techniques lack unifying principle explaining why TTFS SNNs specifically benefit or what fundamental insight connects them

Incomplete theoretical justification: gradient analysis (Figure 5) lacks rigor for explaining vanishing gradient mitigation beyond initialization; no theoretical analysis of normalization stability during training; training/inference asymmetry (Eq. 4: forced firing at T-1) unexplained

Dataset-specific hyperparameter selection: Figure 9 shows temporal decay weight γ varies dramatically (Fashion-MNIST: γ=3 exponential optimal, CIFAR10: γ=3 linear optimal, DVS Gesture: γ=1.5 linear optimal) with no principled selection criterion, limiting generalizability

Incomplete comparisons: Table 1 contrasts direct training with conversion methods using fundamentally different architectures (VGG-16: 138M params vs SCNN: 70M) and propagation modes; practical energy efficiency claimed but not measured

Limited evaluation scope: only simple static datasets (MNIST variants, CIFAR10); DVS Gesture is sole dynamic dataset; no evaluation on larger modern datasets or exploration of efficiency compared to standard ANNs; all networks from prior work, generalization unclear

Methodological concerns: weight normalization application frequency (per-iteration vs per-epoch) unspecified; interaction with surrogate gradients not analyzed; no statistical significance testing, confidence intervals, or multiple runs reported

strengths: Clear identification of signal diminishing problem in Kaiming initialization for TTFS SNNs with empirical validation (Figure 1, 5)
Strong state-of-the-art results on tested benchmarks with substantial improvements (CIFAR10: 90.56% vs 80.0%, DVS Gesture: 95.83%)
Impressive latency reduction through temporal weighting decoding (Table 2: 1.01-2.93 timesteps vs prior 2.93-4.62)
Rigorous mathematical analysis of pooling layers with correct proof that average-pooling preserves one-spike characteristic (Eq. 35-36)
Excellent reproducibility with complete code, trained weights, experimental settings, and comprehensive supplementary materials
Systematic ablation studies (Tables 3, 5) demonstrating incremental contributions of each component
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (Figure 1 overview, Figure 6 distribution shifts)
weaknesses: Critical training-inference mismatch: neurons forced to fire at t=T-1 during training (Eq. 4) but not during inference, creating distribution shift and undermining theoretical justification

Circular reasoning in initialization theory: ETTFS-init derivation assumes one-spike property (Eq. 7) that is only guaranteed by the artificial forced firing mechanism, creating interdependence not adequately discussed

Severely limited experimental scope: only tested on small datasets (MNIST, Fashion-MNIST 28×28, CIFAR10 32×32, DVS Gesture); no ImageNet or large-scale evaluation explicitly deferred to future work, insufficient for ICML

Dataset-specific hyperparameter tuning required: temporal decay parameter γ needs manual selection per dataset (γ=3 exp. for Fashion-MNIST, γ=3 lin. for CIFAR10, γ=1.5 lin. for DVS) with no principled selection strategy
Unfair baseline comparisons: conversion methods use layer-by-layer propagation (different problem paradigm); direct comparison conflates architectural choices rather than methods

Mostly incremental technical contributions: ETTFS-init is straightforward variance scaling once problem identified; weight normalization reuses Salimans & Kingma (2016); temporal weighting uses simple exponential/linear decay; pooling analysis is more observation than innovation
Missing statistical analysis: no error bars, confidence intervals, or multiple runs; some improvements appear marginal (90.56% vs 90.2%) without significance testing
Limited depth testing: only validated up to 11 layers with added 800-unit FC layers; claims about deeper network stability unsupported on genuinely deep modern architectures (ResNets, Transformers)
No computational cost analysis: training overhead from weight normalization and affine transforms not quantified; unclear if convergence speedup justifies added computation
Weight normalization fusion details unclear (Eq. 18): how per-batch normalization is absorbed into weights for inference not adequately explained
Insufficient theoretical justification: why these specific techniques work analyzed only empirically; no principled reasoning for decay function choices or parametrization
Training-inference forcing asymmetry (Eq. 4) feels like engineering hack rather than principled design; biologically implausible artificial constraint
Limited analysis of prior initialization work: quick dismissal of Ding et al. (2022) and Rossbroich et al. (2022) without deep exploration of why their methods fail on TTFS specifically

strengths: Clearly identified and well-motivated problem: diagnoses signal diminishing in TTFS SNNs with rigorous variance analysis (D(X^l) = 1/3T with Kaiming initialization)
Rigorous theoretical foundation: mathematical derivations for ETTFS-init are sound and connection to gradient vanishing is demonstrated empirically (Figure 5)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: thorough ablation studies (Table 3), deep network stability analysis (Figure 7), multiple datasets, and both accuracy and latency metrics
Strong empirical results: achieves state-of-the-art among TTFS SNNs with significant latency reduction (1.01 vs 2.93 time-steps on MNIST)
Excellent reproducibility: complete experimental settings, detailed architectures, promised code/weights enable full replication
Practical pooling analysis: elegantly proves average-pooling preserves one-spike characteristic (Eq. 35-36), addressing real hardware concerns
Clear presentation and well-structured paper with informative figures and generally consistent notation
weaknesses: Limited dataset scope: evaluation restricted to MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR10 (small benchmarks by 2024 standards); no ImageNet or large-scale evaluation; conversion methods still outperform on CIFAR10 (92.72% vs 90.56%)

Hyperparameter sensitivity without principled selection: decay factor γ is highly dataset-dependent (Figure 9, Table 4) with no theoretical guidance or heuristics for new datasets, limiting generalization

Limited novelty in individual components: ETTFS-init is straightforward variance scaling, weight normalization borrowed from prior work [76-78], temporal weighting is natural TTFS extension; contribution is primarily in combination rather than fundamental innovation

Incomplete hardware validation: emphasizes neuromorphic chip deployment but provides no actual energy measurements, hardware results, or experimental validation of step-by-step propagation benefits on real accelerators

Artificial training mechanism not fully justified: Equation (4) forces last-timestep firing during training (differs from inference), and theoretical analysis relies on maintaining one-spike characteristic that is artificially ensured
Missing statistical rigor: no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance testing across multiple runs; some improvements are modest and could benefit from significance analysis
Generalization concerns: methods tightly coupled to TTFS constraint; unclear how techniques transfer to other SNN coding schemes (rate coding, burst coding), limiting broader impact
